opportunities.title: Front-door repair on the 31-page town site: real titles, LocalBusiness schema with the four licence numbers, and a booking path instead of a free-text quote form
opportunities.problem: The site was relaunched around September 2026 with 31 town pages aimed at exactly the searches this firm wants (Milltown, East Brunswick, Edison, Old Bridge, Monroe, Princeton), but the machine-readable layer is missing: the raw HTML title is empty on every page, there is no meta description, zero application/ld+json blocks, and the sitemap lists only the homepage. Legacy .php URLs still indexed by Google now resolve to the same empty single-page shell, and the animated counters read '0' to any text-only reader. So neither Google's snippets nor AI assistants can tell what town or service a page is for, and there is no way to book a service call - only a name/phone/service/free-text quote form.
evidence: Raw HTML <title> is empty, no meta description, and zero application/ld+json on the home page despite full licence and town data being on the page (https://hollanderelectric.com/)
XML sitemap contains only the homepage (lastmod 2026-09-03) although 31 town pages are linked from it (https://hollanderelectric.com/sitemap.xml)
Legacy indexed URLs such as /residential.php now return the same empty-title single-page shell (https://hollanderelectric.com/residential.php)
Animated credential counters render as literal '0' to a text-only reader, so the first thing read is '0 IN BUSINESS SINCE' (https://hollanderelectric.com/electrician/milltown)

Browser triage scored agent readiness findable 3/5, answerable 2/5, bookable 2/5: profile claimed and active, quote form present with no CAPTCHA, but no calendar booking and no schema (https://hollanderelectric.com/)

The '4.8 / 208 reviews' block on the site is static text rather than a live Google feed, though 4.8 from 207 reviews is confirmed on Google (https://www.google.com/maps/place/Hollander+Electric/@40.4835935,-74.497676,10z/data=!4m8!3m7!1s0x89c3c4583c2a3431:0x5f303e8f28a7c110!8m2!3d40.4835935!4d-74.497676!9m1!1b1!16s%2Fg%2F1xg5tmkb)

Correction carried from triage: the 'emoji page title' finding was a browser artefact; the raw HTML title is genuinely empty, which leaves the substance of the finding intact (https://hollanderelectric.com/)
No business hours are published on the site; hours appear only in third-party profiles as Mon-Fri 8:00-4:30 (https://reviews.birdeye.com/hollander-electric-llc-889694528)
opportunities.agent_design: Not an autonomous agent first - a build (capability G) with one thin agent on top. Work items: (1) generate a unique title and meta description per town x service page from the existing on-page copy, and 301 the still-indexed legacy .php URLs onto the matching town/service pages; (2) emit ElectricalContractor/LocalBusiness JSON-LD carrying the four published credentials (NJ Master Electrician #9674, Master HVAC #4711 and #6091, HIC #13VH02466500), the service-area list, the real hours and a live sameAs link to the Google profile, plus aggregateRating pulled from a review feed rather than hard-coded text; (3) rebuild the sitemap to 32+ URLs; (4) replace the free-text quote form with an intake that captures service address, premises type (commercial/industrial/residential), panel or equipment size, urgency and an access window, then an intake agent replies by SMS/email to fill any missing scope fields, proposes two or three call windows from a calendar and creates the job record - a person confirms the slot and any price. Human approval: every quoted price, every dispatch, and any job outside the listed service towns.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: The gap is not copywriting or a chatbot subscription: it needs server-side rendering or prerendering on a Vite/React single-page build, per-page structured data at scale, redirect discipline for 31+ legacy URLs so ranking is not thrown away, and a calendar/job-record write path. A website builder cannot emit or validate the schema, cannot maintain the legacy redirect map, and cannot answer the follow-up questions a commercial service request needs before a truck rolls.

impact_estimate.range: No auditable dollar benchmark exists, so no revenue figure is claimed. What customers and answer engines see today, measured: 32/32 crawled URLs carry no title text, 0 JSON-LD blocks, 0 bookable slots, and hours visible only on third-party profiles. Target after the fix: 32 titled pages, 1 ElectricalContractor schema type with 4 licence IDs, and a booking request path that captures service address and urgency; delivery effort is about 1-2 days for titles/schema/redirects plus about 1 week for the booking intake.
impact_estimate.assumptions: Assumes current SERP/answer-engine invisibility is the binding constraint on the 31 town pages (inference: no page titles or schema were observed, and the pages are not in the sitemap). No analytics, Search Console or call-volume data was available, so traffic and revenue lift are left unmodelled on purpose. The redirect and schema work is small and mechanical, per the triage effort rating of S.

opportunities.pilot_scope: 2 weeks: full technical audit of all 32 URLs; unique titles and meta descriptions live on all town pages; ElectricalContractor JSON-LD with the four licence numbers, hours and service-area on every page; 301 map for indexed legacy .php URLs; regenerated sitemap; validation in Search Console and a rich-results test; plus a 5-field booking request that writes to a shared calendar and notifies the owner, with a scripted SMS follow-up for missing scope details.

opportunities.title: 24/7 emergency and overflow intake desk that triages the call, captures site and panel details, and escalates to the on-call electrician for human acceptance
opportunities.problem: The firm sells 24/7 emergency response to commercial and industrial clients and a same-business-day response to web requests, but the web channel is a form reviewed in office hours and published hours are Mon-Fri 8:00-4:30. Reviewers describe the owner personally answering a Friday call and taking the details, which means the after-hours promise runs through one or two mobile phones. The quote form captures only name, phone, service dropdown, town and free text - no service address, no panel or service size, no outage scope, no access window, no urgency field and no calendar handoff - so every serious lead costs a callback to scope, and a 3 a.m. 'switchgear is arcing' call and a 'quote for a panel upgrade' call arrive the same way.
evidence: Site advertises 24/7 emergency response for commercial and industrial clients and a same-business-day response on web quote requests (https://hollanderelectric.com/)
Published hours are Mon-Fri 8:00-4:30 with weekends closed, and they appear only in third-party profiles, not on the site (https://reviews.birdeye.com/hollander-electric-llc-889694528)

Web intake is three plain forms plus tel: links; the quote form asks name, phone, service dropdown, town and a free-text 'how can we help?' - no address, panel data or scheduling (https://hollanderelectric.com/)

A reviewer describes calling on a Friday and 'the owner answered, took my information' and booked a Monday visit, i.e. intake is owner-level and manual (https://www.google.com/maps/place/Hollander+Electric/@40.4835935,-74.497676,10z/data=!4m8!3m7!1s0x89c3c4583c2a3431:0x5f303e8f28a7c110!8m2!3d40.4835935!4d-74.497676!9m1!1b1!16s%2Fg%2F1xg5tmkb)

Google review topic chips group 'promptness' (9 mentions) and 'courteous staff' (7), so responsiveness is the marketed differentiator that any intake change must protect (https://www.google.com/maps/place/Hollander+Electric/@40.4835935,-74.497676,10z/data=!4m8!3m7!1s0x89c3c4583c2a3431:0x5f303e8f28a7c110!8m2!3d40.4835935!4d-74.497676!9m1!1b1!16s%2Fg%2F1xg5tmkb)
No booking widget, chat widget, CRM or dispatch integration is visible anywhere on the page, so there is no system of record for inbound demand to fall into (https://hollanderelectric.com/)

Analogue evidence: an NBER working paper (w31161, later published in QJE) found a generative-AI assistant raised issues resolved per hour by 14% across 5,179 customer-support agents, with 34% gains for novices - a working paper on support work, not a contractor field study (https://www.nber.org/papers/w31161)
opportunities.agent_design: A voice and SMS agent answering the published number when the office is closed and on overflow during the day, plus an instant reply to every web form submission. Triggers: inbound call outside 8:00-4:30, second concurrent call, unanswered ring after N seconds, or a new form/email lead. Flow: confirm business vs residential and the town against the published service-area list; capture service address, premises type, what is down or arcing or hot, panel/service size and amperage if the caller knows it, generator/standby status, access constraints (gate code, dock, super, escort), callback number and photo request by SMS; classify P1 (no power, burning smell, arcing, generator failure at a commercial site) vs P2 (quote, upgrade, PM visit). P1 pages the on-call technician with the structured summary and waits for a human 'accept' before committing an overtime call-out. P2 writes a job record with the missing scope fields and offers two or three call windows. System touches: telephony/SMS provider, calendar, email, and whatever CRM or field-service tool is chosen as the record. Human approval: all after-hours dispatch and overtime, all pricing, anything outside the service towns or needing a permit judgment.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: Off-the-shelf AI answering services read a script and take a message; this design has to hold a service-area and licensing model, branch on urgency for high-voltage commercial equipment, write structured records into a job system, and gate an on-call escalation on a human acceptance. It also sits on regulated ground: no remote diagnosis presented as advice, no card data over voice (PCI), call-recording consent, and job notes that must stay attributable and editable because they feed permits, warranties and insurance claims.

impact_estimate.range: USD 3,000-9,000 per year of recovered office time, plus an unquantified recovery of after-hours jobs that currently reach voicemail. Arithmetic: about 480-720 intake, triage and callback hours per year (inference of 10-15 hrs/week x 48 weeks) cost USD 11,000-18,900 at NJ medians of USD 22.95/hr (customer service reps, USD 47,740) to USD 26.25/hr (dispatchers, USD 54,590); deflecting 30-50% of first-pass work gives the range. The 14% issues-per-hour gain in the NBER working paper is the directional analogue, not a multiplier applied here.
impact_estimate.assumptions: Headcount is unverified (a LinkedIn snippet reporting 2-10 employees could not be opened) and no call volume, form volume or labour hours were available, so call and lead counts are inferred from a family-sized firm where the owner answers the phone. Wage figures are BLS OEWS May 2025 annual medians for New Jersey, gross wage only (add roughly 25-35% for payroll burden to reach true cost). No revenue is attributed to recovered after-hours calls because no defensible close-rate or average-ticket benchmark exists.

opportunities.pilot_scope: 3-4 weeks: one published number with after-hours and overflow answering, a triage script covering six job types (service upgrade, panel/breaker, three-phase distribution fault, lighting controls, standby generator, EV charger), P1 escalation to on-call with human acceptance, structured job records written to a shared sheet or existing tool, and a weekly report of calls handled, P1s escalated, callbacks avoided and transcripts for tuning. Success criteria agreed up front: no P1 left unhandled, and the owner's callback queue shorter at the end than at the start.

opportunities.title: Service-watch: read-only condition monitoring on the preventive-maintenance book, with an agent turning panel and generator drift into reviewed service tickets
opportunities.problem: Preventive maintenance and 24/7 standby-power service are sold to industrial and facility clients, but the visible toolset is a marketing site plus a review platform: no monitoring, telemetry or field-service system is exposed anywhere public. Inference: PM visits are calendar-driven, so a failing contactor, a drifting phase imbalance or a generator that keeps failing its weekly exercise is found on the next scheduled visit or when the customer calls in an emergency - which is precisely the 24/7 line the firm has to staff. The business-specific part of this opportunity rests on inference; what is verified is the service mix (switchgear, motor controls, standby power, generators, EV charging), the four master licences that let the firm install and service this itself, and field work at plants and motor-control rooms.
evidence: Commercial/industrial electrical is the stated primary focus - three-phase distribution, panelboards/switchgear/transformers, motor controls, generators, standby power, EV charging (https://hollanderelectric.com/)

Offers a preventive-maintenance program for industrial facilities plus NEIF/JCP&L-backed financing, which points to recurring contract work rather than one-off jobs (https://www.neifund.org/hollander-electric-llc/)
Holds NJ Master Electrician #9674 and two Master HVAC licences (#4711, #6091), so electrical installation and HVAC-side diagnosis can be self-performed (https://hollanderelectric.com/)

Work is field-based at commercial/industrial sites - office, retail and restaurant fit-outs, plants, switchgear and motor-control rooms - with crews 'on the road every day' (https://hollanderelectric.com/electrician/milltown)

No fleet size, shop, warehouse or square footage is published, and the street address comes only from a third-party profile, so there is no owned facility to instrument - the assets are the customers' (https://reviews.birdeye.com/hollander-electric-llc-889694528)

Method evidence, small and non-peer-reviewed: an arXiv preprint (2017) applied cohort-dissimilarity machine learning to one year of data from 17 HVAC systems in an Italian hospital and reached AUC up to 0.96 for certain fault types - a preprint with a small, non-residential cohort, cited as method support only (https://arxiv.org/abs/1701.03633)
opportunities.agent_design: Retrofit read-only sensors at two or three PM-contract customer sites: clamp-on current transformers and contact-temperature sensors at panelboards and motor-control centres, plus generator battery/annunciator and exercise-cycle signals where the controller exposes them, on a cellular gateway (or the site's existing BMS where one exists). The agent baselines each circuit per site, flags drift and anomalies (phase imbalance, rising contactor temperature, a generator that failed its weekly exercise, load creep on a service), opens a service ticket addressed to a named Hollander person, drafts the customer-facing PM report, and proposes whether the issue belongs in the next PM visit or needs an earlier trip. Every alert is advisory and reviewed by a person before the customer hears anything; there is no automated accusation, no camera, no audio and no biometric identification - the purpose is equipment and operations, not security, so it does not fall under the alarm-business licensing triggered for CCTV, access control and physical-security AI, and installation of the sensors is electrical work done by the firm's licensed master electrician. If any design later drifts toward intrusion or surveillance, a licensed alarm or electrical contractor installs it and staff notice and signage follow the state rules.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: This is hardware plus telemetry plus a model plus a workflow: sensor selection and installation in live panels, a gateway and data pipeline at third-party sites, per-site baselining where there is no history, alert-threshold tuning to avoid alarm fatigue, and integration into how tickets get created. No chatbot subscription touches it, and the data is the customers' equipment data, so the privacy and consent terms have to be written for a commercial client, not a consumer app.

impact_estimate.range: No measured contractor ROI exists, so no dollar figure is claimed. Conservative target for a 2-3 site pilot: 5-20 electrician-hours of avoided emergency or repeat-visit labour per instrumented site-year (inference), i.e. roughly USD 185-740 per site-year at the NJ electrician median of USD 77,250 (about USD 37/hr gross wage, before burden and before any billable-rate multiplier) - small on its own. The real case is retention and upsell of monitored PM contracts, which cannot be quantified from public data.
impact_estimate.assumptions: Assumes customers consent to instrumentation, that electrical rooms have cellular coverage or an accessible BMS, and that spare CT/breaker space exists - all unverified. Assumes PM contract count and value are unknown (none published). Method evidence is a 2017 arXiv preprint on 17 HVAC systems in one hospital, so it supports feasibility of cohort-based fault detection, not an expected catch rate. Sensor and gateway hardware cost is unquoted and excluded.

opportunities.pilot_scope: 4 weeks at one willing PM customer: 2-3 panelboards plus the standby generator instrumented, 30-60 days of baseline, an agent that converts drift into a reviewed ticket and a one-page PM report. Success = at least one genuine pre-failure catch (or a clean, honest negative result), fewer than one false alert per week after tuning, and a report the customer would pay for. Kill the idea if the first site cannot be instrumented or tuned inside the pilot.
walk_in_checks: Which customers are on a written PM contract, how many, and what the contract promises (visit frequency, response time, who owns the generator)
Whether any PM contract already has a monitoring or remote-diagnostics clause that would make an offer easy to attach
Spare physical space in panelboards and MCCs for clamp-on CTs, and whether panels are live-work restricted or need a shutdown window
Cellular signal strength inside electrical rooms and generator enclosures; whether a BMS/BAS exists with a usable open protocol
Generator controller make and age - whether exercise status and fault codes are readable without a vendor licence
Who at a customer site signs off on installing third-party sensors, and whether leases or landlords block it
Whether the owner has ever lost or nearly lost a PM customer after an unplanned failure - the real buying trigger
Current PM paperwork: what a delivered PM report looks like today and who writes it

lead_score.rationale: Pain 25/30: the front door is measurably broken - empty titles, zero JSON-LD, a homepage-only sitemap, 301-less legacy URLs and no booking - and the 24/7 emergency promise is backed by a business-hours form and the owner's mobile; the internal operations pain (callbacks, PM paperwork) is inference, not measured, and the review sample shows no cluster of missed-call complaints, so it is not higher. Fit 17/20: G and A are squarely in scope, and the E design matches the equipment-and-flow preference rather than surveillance. Ability to pay 14/20: 38 years trading, four master licences, commercial/industrial work and NEIF/JCP&L financing argue for real revenue, but headcount is unverified (2-10 per an unopenable LinkedIn snippet) and no owned facility is published. Ease 10/15: the front-door fix is a day or two, but the intake desk and especially the sensor pilot need customer cooperation. Strategic 12/15: front-door plus intake is a repeatable playbook for the thousands of small NJ electrical/HVAC contractors, and monitored PM is a differentiator, though slower to replicate. On E: no avenues.json was supplied in this folder, so no verified avenue could be used; profile.json does show a physical operation (field crews at plants, switchgear and motor-control rooms, 24/7 standby-power service), but there is no owned shop, yard or warehouse to instrument and the assets belong to customers - that is why E is kept as the third and highest-risk opportunity rather than the first, built on the firm's PM and generator book, with its business-specific parts labelled inference and walk-in checks attached. Note that the strongest measured automation evidence available is a working paper on customer-support work, not a contractor field study, so impact figures are labour-time arithmetic, not measured outcomes.

best_evidence_signal: It advertises 24/7 emergency response for commercial and industrial clients while the only web channel is a same-business-day quote form and its hours (Mon-Fri 8:00-4:30) appear only on third-party profiles - https://hollanderelectric.com/
suggested_channel: phone - the owner answers the main line himself per a reviewer, so call 732-940-0101; email toby@hollanderelectric.com as backup since no street address is published
